q: What defines Gothic architecture?
n: Pointed arches, rib vaults, flying buttresses.

q: Which of the following is true about Gothic architecture?
n: Gothic churches use rib vaults and spires rather than domes.

q: Flying buttresses are typical of which style?
n: They let Gothic walls open up for glass.

q: Which style is referred to as the architecture of geometry due to its strong emphasis on proportion and symmetry?
n: Gothic design rests on geometric proportion (ad quadratum, ad triangulum).

q: In architecture, Gothic art was considered the most ___ of its time.
n: Gothic architecture is often described as the most intellectual art of its age, tied to scholasticism.

q: In Gothic architecture, which English style is considered closest to the French style?
n: English Decorated Gothic parallels the French Rayonnant style.

q: What was the most common building stone of French Gothic?
n: The Paris basin and northern France are rich in limestone.

q: Which description was historically attached to Gothic architecture by its critics?
n: Renaissance writers named it after the "barbarian" Goths.

q: In French, "l'architecture ogivale" refers to:
n: Ogive means pointed arch or rib.

q: Which style is famous for gargoyles?
n: Carved spouts throw rainwater off the roof.

q: What architectural innovation was introduced in Gothic walls?
n: Thin walls between buttresses opened up to far more glass.

q: What architectural feature became possible in Gothic cathedrals due to new structural support methods?
n: Flying buttresses let walls be opened up into many large windows.

q: Which style reached new heights in verticality?
n: Tall naves and spires.

q: What is a continuous row of arches called?
n: A colonnade carries beams, not arches.

q: What is the upper wall with windows rising above an adjacent roof?
n: It lights the nave from above the aisles.

q: What decorative open-timber roof truss of English Gothic uses short brackets projecting from the wall?
n: Westminster Hall has the classic hammerbeam roof.

q: Which Marian pilgrimage cathedral is known for its three west-front portals (the Royal Portal)?
n: Chartres's Royal Portal dates to about 1145.

q: What is the gallery opening onto the nave at an upper level, below the clerestory?
n: The triforium runs over the arcade.

q: Which building is a splendid example of Early Gothic architecture?
n: Notre-Dame de Paris (begun 1163) is a prime Early Gothic example.

q: Which Christopher Wren cathedral has a large central space under its dome for big congregations?
n: St. Paul's, London, finished in 1710.

q: Which cathedral has the "Five Sisters" window?
n: Five tall grisaille lancets in the north transept.

q: How many years did it take to build the Notre Dame Cathedral in Paris?
n: Notre-Dame took about 182 years (1163–1345).

q: What is the tallest church in the world today?
n: In October 2025 the Sagrada Família (162.91 m) passed Ulm Minster (161.53 m).

q: Which Gothic cathedral has the longest nave among Gothic churches?
n: Winchester Cathedral has the longest Gothic nave in Europe.

q: Which cathedral has 176 stained-glass windows?
n: Chartres keeps most of its medieval glass.

q: Which Romanesque cathedral has twin towers, a dome and apses at both ends?
n: A double-ended Rhenish cathedral.

q: Which Italian Renaissance palace is built of brick and features quoining on the corners?
n: Palazzo Farnese is brick with stone quoins at its corners.

q: What is the most influential building of the Byzantine period?
n: Its domed space set the model.

q: Cologne Cathedral, begun in 1248 and finished in 1880, took about how many years?
Which church is known for being a ‘Half Gothic, Half Renaissance’ architectural style?
n: Granada Cathedral was begun Gothic and finished Renaissance.

q: Which cathedral has the "Smiling Angel" sculpture at its doorway?
n: L'Ange au Sourire is on Reims's west front.

q: Which cathedral has two west towers of different designs?
n: A Romanesque spire and a Flamboyant one.

q: Which church features twin towers of the same design but different heights?
n: Chartres has two spires of different design and height.

q: Which style name means "Roman-like"?
n: It used Roman round arches and vaults.

q: Which vault was widely used in Romanesque churches to carry stone roofs?
n: The barrel (tunnel) vault.
